evidence.P1: The Reluctant One chain holds causal integrity well: ev-038 (Neo refuses to run) is genuinely raised into necessity by ev-037 (Smith's point-blank trap), and ev-045 (seizing identity) is caused by ev-044 (death/revival) — but ev-020 and ev-022 lean on 'priming' and 'vulnerability' rather than strict causation, softening the chain at the midpoint.
evidence.P2: The Reluctant One plot is disciplined as one stance (identity accepted by faith vs. refusal), and The Betrayer holds a clean counter-position (pleasure over struggle); but The Hunter and the Chosen drifts into a retelling of the Reluctant One's climax (ev-039 refusal, ev-045 destruction) rather than sustaining a distinct dilemma-stance, and The Rescue overlaps the same beats (ev-032, ev-034, ev-035) as a society-frame of what is fundamentally the Reluctant One's wager.
evidence.P3: The Awakening to the Real chain is well-populated and each event earns its place (ev-004 → ev-006 → ev-007 → ev-008 → ev-009 → ev-010 → ev-011 → ev-012 → ev-013 is a tight, unbroken sequence); but The Hunter and the Chosen is under-populated — it skips the entire Agent-enforcement spine (ev-001, ev-018, ev-031, ev-037, ev-043) and rests on only four events, leaving the 'hunter' half of its own thesis largely uncited.
evidence.P4: The Reluctant One arc is complete: seed (ev-008 naming), escalating refusals (ev-014, ev-015, ev-016, ev-020, ev-022, ev-032), first turn toward embodiment (ev-038, ev-039), annihilation (ev-044), and resolution (ev-045) — nothing dangles; The Awakening similarly completes setup→choice→consequence→payoff cleanly.
evidence.P5: The Rescue and The Reluctant One both claim ev-032 ('a wager on a man rather than a prophecy'), ev-034, and ev-035 as their own — the same events doing double thematic work; and The Hunter and the Chosen re-hashes ev-039 and ev-045 already resolved in The Reluctant One, so three of the five plots materially overlap rather than partition the event-spool.

raw.commentary: The layer's strongest plot is The Reluctant One, whose chain is causally sound and arc-complete, and The Awakening to the Real, which is tightly sequenced and non-redundant. Its weakness is structural overlap: The Rescue is essentially the Reluctant One's midpoint reframed through 'society,' and The Hunter and the Chosen re-litigates the Reluctant One's climax under a freedom/determinism banner while under-citing its own enforcement spine. The result is five plots where two or three are doing redundant work on the same events, and one (Hunter) is too thin to stand apart. Membership is uneven — full in the Awakening chain, sparse in the Hunter chain.
